title: 通胀五年超标：美联储为何按兵不动，前央行行长拉詹应继续加息？
speaker: Bloomberg

segments.en: Professor Rajan, all is going to have you with us. We know that three federal officials are already saying that inflation remains way too high
segments.zh: 拉詹教授，欢迎您。我们知道已有三位美联储官员表示通胀仍然过高。

segments.en: right now. Is there a sense perhaps that wash maybe underestimating how entrenched inflation has become?
segments.zh: 是否有可能低估了通胀的顽固程度？

segments.en: I don't think he's underestimating it. After all, he's been on record saying it's been too high for too long, five years of
segments.zh: 我不认为他低估了。毕竟他公开表示通胀过高已持续太久，五年了。

segments.en: above target inflation. So I don't think he fully understands the need to get it under control.
segments.zh: 他完全理解控制通胀的必要性。

segments.en: He fully understands the magnitude of the task that is needed and certainly doesn't want inflation to be for another so many months above target.
segments.zh: 他清楚任务的艰巨，当然不希望通胀再持续数月高于目标。

segments.en: So why is he waiting? We have the likes of Jeffrey Schmidt questioning whether you know three and a half or three point seven five percent policy is tight enough whether it is effective in raining in inflation.
segments.zh: 那他为何等待？像杰弗里·施密特等人质疑3.5%或3.75%的政策利率是否足够紧缩，能否有效抑制通胀。

segments.en: Well clearly the labor market has been somewhat weaker recently.
segments.zh: 显然，近期劳动力市场有所走弱。

segments.en: There is also some thought that when you look at the fed zone measure of inflation PC core,
segments.zh: 也有人认为，美联储关注的PCE核心通胀指标，

segments.en: it is somewhat above other measures of inflation.
